race.name: GFNY República Dominicana
race.tagline: A fast 144.6-kilometer Caribbean gran fondo built around coastal wind, rolling roads, and bunch positioning.

vitals.field_size: The organizer has not published a 2026 field cap.
vitals.start_format: Caribbean Lake Park opens to riders from 4:30-6:00am; corrals close at 6:15am and the race starts at 6:30am. The rules order VIP and competitive corrals first, then general long-course riders by age group, medium-course riders, and para-athletes.
vitals.registration: Riders must be 18 or older. In-person packet pickup is Saturday, September 12 from 11:00am-6:00pm at Caribbean Lake Park; the organizer says riders cannot race without their packet. The current-year GFNY jersey is mandatory on race day.
vitals.entry_fee: $185 standard entry plus an $18.50 service fee as displayed August 15, 2026; GFNY uses changing sales periods, so recheck the live registration widget.
vitals.feed_zones: The rules refer to organizer aid stations and eco zones, but the organizer has not published the 2026 station locations or contents.
vitals.cutoff_time: No rider cutoff is published. The official schedule estimates all cyclists arriving by 1:00pm; that estimate is not a stated cutoff.
route_options: Long: 144.6 km / 89.9 mi, 647 m / 2,123 ft — timed competitive course with category rankings and awards
Medium: 95.9 km / 59.6 mi — timed, but results are alphabetical and riders are not ranked; elevation is not published

climate.description: A September race in Punta Cana with coastal wind explicitly identified by the organizer as a course feature. Heat and humidity preparation is prudent, but race-day weather must be checked close to the event rather than inferred from climatology.
challenges: Exposed coastal wind on a speed-oriented course
Potential tropical heat and humidity; the organizer has not published a race-day forecast

terrain.surface: Paved road course. The organizer describes a wide, multi-lane opening before the route turns north through rural roads, short punchy rollers, Uvero Alto, Las Lagunas de Nisibón, and El Cedro. It does not publish a full road-surface audit.
features: Wide multi-lane opening where the peloton can organize
Short, punchy rollers rather than sustained climbs
Rural roads through Uvero Alto, Las Lagunas de Nisibón, and El Cedro
Coastal wind and exposed speed sections

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Regraded August 15, 2026 against the official 2026 relaunch, course, schedule, rules, registration, travel, and hotel pages. The old 99.8 km / 1,067 m profile was obsolete. Distance 4->3 follows the 120-160 km rubric for the official 144.6 km long course; climbing 3->2 follows the 500-1,500 m rubric for 647 m. Descent technicality 2->1 reflects the organizer's wide-road, short-roller description. Logistics 4->1 reflects PUJ 15 minutes from Punta Cana and abundant organizer-listed lodging. Road surface 1->2 avoids claiming fresh tarmac throughout when no full surface audit is published. Organization 4->2, community 4->2, and scenery 4->3 are conservative because the event is relaunching under renewed organization and the 2026 edition has not yet occurred; the rules also require obeying normal road controls unless police override them, so full closure is not claimed. Expenses 2->4 reflects destination travel, while cultural impact 3->2 reflects a returning international-brand event without evidence of deep local cycling heritage. Overall score recalculated 64->51; tier changes T2->T3. Regrade after the 2026 event with results, rider reports, and final operational evidence.

course_description.character: A long, fast Caribbean road race with only 647 meters of climbing across 144.6 kilometers. The wide opening favors a quick peloton, then short rollers, rural roads, and coastal wind create repeated positioning and pacing decisions rather than sustained mountain climbing.
course_description.signature_challenge: Maintaining aerodynamic speed and bunch position for nearly 145 kilometers without overreacting to every short rise or wind-driven acceleration. The course rewards durable tempo, repeatable surges, fueling discipline, and competent group riding.
suffering_zones: The fast multi-lane opening, where poor positioning can force repeated costly accelerations before the race settles.
The northern rolling sector toward El Cedro, where short punchy rises interrupt rhythm and expose riders who surge above threshold too often.
Late exposed kilometers back toward Punta Cana, where accumulated fatigue, coastal wind, and dwindling groups can turn a fast course into a long solo effort.

logistics.airport: Punta Cana International Airport (PUJ). The organizer says PUJ is about 15 minutes from the Punta Cana area and serves direct flights from more than 28 countries and 96 cities; Santo Domingo (SDQ) is also included in the event's United travel window.
logistics.lodging_strategy: The organizer lists several bike-friendly host hotels, including properties that allow bikes in rooms and guarantee a 4:00am race-day breakfast. Confirm the hotel's bike policy if booking elsewhere.
logistics.transport: Race-week group rides, Saturday expo and packet pickup, Sunday start/finish, post-race meal, and awards are all scheduled at Caribbean Lake Park. The organizer lists 24-hour airport taxis and rental-car desks; it specifically warns that JetBlue does not transport bicycles to the Dominican Republic.
logistics.food: The post-race meal is scheduled to begin at 10:00am at Caribbean Lake Park. Aid-station locations and contents are not yet published.

history.origin_story: GFNY first brought its mass-participation road format to Punta Cana in 2019. GFNY announced a 2026 return under renewed organization after an absence from the calendar.
notable_moments: First staged in Punta Cana in 2019
Officially relaunched for September 13, 2026 with a new 144.6 km long course and 95.9 km medium course
The long course is competitive and ranked; the medium course is timed but explicitly non-competitive

biased_opinion.summary: GFNY Dominican Republic is a speed-and-wind race, not a climbing fondo. The 144.6 km long course is substantial, but 647 m of climbing means the decisive demands are likely to be group position, repeated short surges, aerodynamic durability, fueling, and handling exposed wind. Punta Cana makes the trip easy by destination-race standards. The caution is equally important: this is a 2026 relaunch, the current course page conflicts with the press release and schedule on the exact start wording, and final aid-station and cutoff details are not published.
strengths: Competitive long course with structured age-group rankings
Fast rolling course with coastal scenery and a genuinely distinct wind-racing demand
International airport and extensive bike-friendly lodging close to race week
weaknesses: 2026 relaunch has no completed-edition evidence under the renewed organization
Current official pages conflict on Downtown Punta Cana versus Caribbean Lake Park start wording
Aid-station details and a rider cutoff are not yet published
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Choose it for fast Caribbean road racing and destination convenience, not for mountain climbing; recheck the final race guide before travel and race week.

final_verdict.one_liner: A convenient Caribbean destination race whose real difficulty is sustaining speed and position across 144.6 wind-exposed kilometers.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race the long course if you want structured age-group competition on a fast, rolling Caribbean route and are comfortable in a peloton. Choose the 95.9 km medium course if you want a timed ride without competitive rankings. Do not buy it as a climbing objective: the official long route has 647 m of gain. Because the 2026 event is a relaunch and key operational details remain unpublished, treat the current schedule as provisional and recheck the final race guide, start location, aid stations, and any cutoff before departure.

eligibility.notes: GFNY officially relaunched the Punta Cana / República Dominicana edition for Sunday, September 13, 2026. The official press release publishes 144.6 km and 647 m for the competitive long course and 95.9 km for the recreational medium course. The current official pages contain a start-location conflict: the press release and race-week schedule place the start/finish at Caribbean Lake Park, while the course prose says the route begins in Downtown Punta Cana. Use Caribbean Lake Park for current logistics but recheck the final race guide before race week. The Race Guide link currently redirects to stale Cap Cana material and is not treated as 2026 evidence.
